raises: S97, from my own self-audit lane
method: arithmetic on the declared shapes of the real substrate. Shapes were read from the dictionaries and the availability header; no payload was materialised and no statistic was computed.
findings: The design tensor dominates: 10,552,158 (donor, pair) cells x 14 terms x 8 bytes is 1.10 GB, and the implementation holds up to three of them live at once -- the tensor, its flattened view and the boolean-masked copy the ridge is fitted on. That is 3.30 GB of the 4.90 GB total before any fold slice is taken.

The calculated peak fits within 80 percent of currently available memory, but this is arithmetic on declared shapes, not a measured peak, and it ignores allocator fragmentation and whatever else is running. It is a feasibility indication, not a guarantee.
